title: Localization and boundary comparison for a closed section with a retraction
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum of [def-pur-conventions], with $A=A_{E,n}$. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $p:X\to Y$ be a separated finite-type morphism, and let $s:Y\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed section, so $ps=\operatorname{id}_Y$. Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be its quasi-compact open complement and put $\pi=pj$. The meanings of these morphisms are [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion] and [def-weil-open-immersion]. For each scheme $T$ write $\nu_T:T_{\mathrm{proet}}\to T_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the site comparison [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $B\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and put $K=\nu_X^*B$, in the ordinary module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], where $D^+$ denotes objects whose cohomology sheaves vanish below some integer. Use the finite direct images of [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. Use the finite-level transported exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and put $C=Rs^!K\in D^+(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$.

There is a natural distinguished triangle [def-weil-triangulated-category]
$$C\longrightarrow Rp_*K\longrightarrow R\pi_*j^*K\xrightarrow{d}C[1].$$
It is the $\nu_Y^*$-transport of the ordinary etale closed-support localization triangle after $Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}$, with $Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}s_*s^\times B=s^\times B$. The finite direct-image comparison identifies the second arrow with restriction along $j$. Here $s^\times$ is the ordinary etale right adjoint of $s_*$, and the first arrow is the image of its counit, with the transported exceptional functor and counit identified by the compactification $Y\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}Y\xrightarrow{s}X$. These identifications are natural in $B$ and use the canonical etale/pro-etale direct-image comparisons, rather than an adjunction on all pro-etale inputs.

Use cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] and supported cohomology [def-pur-support-cohomology]. Applying derived global sections to this triangle identifies $H^{q+1}(Y,C)$ with $H^{q+1}_{s(Y)}(X,K)$ and identifies $H^q(Y,d)$ with the support boundary $\partial:H^q(U,j^*K)\to H^{q+1}_{s(Y)}(X,K)$ of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness]. For the canonical edge maps $e_V^r:H^r(Y,V)\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal H^r(V))$ and the cohomology-sheaf boundary $\delta^q:\mathcal H^q(R\pi_*j^*K)\to\mathcal H^{q+1}(C)$, one has, for every integer $q$ and $\alpha\in H^q(U,j^*K)$,
$$e_C^{q+1}(\partial\alpha)=\Gamma(Y,\delta^q)\bigl(e_{R\pi_*j^*K}^{q}(\alpha)\bigr).$$
The edge maps here send a global cohomology class to its local cohomology classes in the cohomology sheaf. The boundary and all these identifications agree with their ordinary etale counterparts under site comparison.

source.place: Unit sk-prop-a1, proof: localization triangle after Rp_*; comparison and edge compatibility expanded from the prior item proof step 2

proof.text:
Put $D=s^	imes B$ on the etale site. The section is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Its compactification $Y\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}Y\xrightarrow{s}X$ therefore gives, by the compactification formula [def-amb-etale-compact-support], $Rs_!^{\mathrm{et}}=Rs_{\mathrm{et},*}$, the K-injective total derived direct image. This is the termwise $s_*$ of [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle]: a closed immersion is affine and given on affine opens by surjective, hence integral, ring maps [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], so $s_*$ is exact on etale abelian sheaves [sbc-lem-integral-etale-direct-image-exact], hence on $A$-module sheaves, whose kernels and cokernels have the underlying abelian kernels and cokernels. By [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] termwise $s_*$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms, so for a K-injective resolution $L	o I$ of any complex $L$ on $Y$ the map $s_*L	o s_*I$ is a quasi-isomorphism, giving $s_*L\cong Rs_{\mathrm{et},*}L$ naturally on the whole unbounded $D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Uniqueness of right adjoints [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] identifies the right adjoint of $Rs_!^{\mathrm{et}}$ with the closed adjoint of that triangle, compatibly with counits. By the finite definition [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and the comparison unit [sk-prop-sf-comparison],
$$C=
u_Y^*s^	imes R
u_{X,*}
u_X^*B\cong
u_Y^*D.$$
In particular $D$ and $C$ are bounded below, with no constructibility assumption. All these identifications are natural in $B$.

source.place: First displayed localization triangle; identify the closed adjoint through the identity/proper compactification

proof.text:
Apply the etale localization triangle [lem-exc-closed-support-triangle] to $B$, and apply $Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}$. This preserves the distinguished triangle and its shift by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. The etale clause and identity law of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition], applied to $(s,p)$ and $(j,p)$, identify its three objects with
$$D,\quad Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}B,\quad R\pi_{\mathrm{et},*}j_{\mathrm{et}}^*B.$$
Indeed $Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}s_*D=R(ps)_{\mathrm{et},*}D=D$. Its first arrow is $Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}$ of the closed counit; its second is $Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}$ of the open unit. Keep its third arrow with the shift comparison supplied by the triangulated functor.

source.place: First paragraph: apply Rp_* to localization and use ps=id

proof.text:
Apply exact $\nu_Y^*$ to the triangle in step 2. It is triangulated by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]; exactness on these module coefficients and pullback commutation are supplied by [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison]. Apply that node's bounded-below direct-image comparisons to $p,\pi$, and $j$. Their hypotheses hold: $p$ is separated finite type, $j$ is a quasi-compact open immersion, and $\pi=pj$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; the same holds for the closed immersion $s$. The pullback comparison gives $j^*K=\nu_U^*j_{\mathrm{et}}^*B$. Together with step 1 these isomorphisms give exactly
$$C\longrightarrow Rp_*K\longrightarrow R\pi_*j^*K\xrightarrow{d}C[1].$$
The comparison's compatibility with units and composition identifies the second arrow with restriction. Its counit compatibility identifies the first arrow with the transported closed counit. This defines $d$, including its sign, by transport of the entire triangle.

source.place: First displayed triangle and its second arrow; finite etale/pro-etale transport

proof.text:
To compare with supported cohomology on the pro-etale site, denote by $S$ the closed support right adjoint on $D^+$ in [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle]. This is temporary notation distinct from the transported $Rs^!$ of the statement. Before applying $Rp_*$, step 3's comparison for $s$ gives a triangle with first object $s_*\nu_Y^*D$ and middle object $K$, whose arrow to $Rj_*j^*K$ is the open unit. Compare it with
$$s_*SK\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K\longrightarrow(s_*SK)[1]$$
from that support-localization node. Rotate both triangles. Their middle-to-open square consists of identity maps, so (TR3) of [def-weil-triangulated-category] supplies a morphism of the rotated triangles. Rotating back gives a map $\lambda:s_*\nu_Y^*D\to s_*SK$ commuting with both the counit arrow to $K$ and the boundary. The other two components are identities, hence $\lambda$ is an isomorphism by [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso].

source.place: Localization triangle, comparison of its first term with the support object

proof.text:
The map just obtained is canonical. The functors $s^*,s_*$ are exact on module sheaves and $s^*s_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]; their derived adjunction is [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Thus termwise counit $s^*s_*\to\mathrm{id}$ stays invertible in the derived categories, and $s_*$ is fully faithful there. Write $\lambda=s_*\theta$. Commutation with the arrow to $K$ says
$$\varepsilon_{S,K}\circ s_*\theta=\varepsilon'_B,$$
where $\varepsilon'_B:s_*\nu_Y^*D\to K$ is the transported etale counit. The adjunction $s_*\dashv S$ in [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle] makes $\theta$ the unique transpose of $\varepsilon'_B$. Consequently $\theta$ is natural in $B$, independent of the TR3 extension, and invertible since $\lambda$ is invertible and $s^*s_*=\mathrm{id}$. Its triangle compatibility, already furnished in step 4, includes the third arrow. Hence $C\cong SK$ identifies the whole transported triangle with the pro-etale support triangle after $Rp_*$, with exactly the same boundary.

source.place: Localization triangle: canonical identification of the supported first term and boundary

proof.text: Here is the resolution computation of its global supported term. Write $s^!_0M=s^*\mathcal G_ZM$, $Z=s(Y)$, as in [def-pur-flasque-support]. For any sheaf $N$ on $Y$, a map $s_*N\to M$ has zero composite to $j_*j^*M$: by the open adjunction this composite corresponds to a map from $j^*s_*N=0$ [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed]. It therefore factors uniquely through $\mathcal G_ZM=s_*s^!_0M$. Full faithfulness of $s_*$ gives $\operatorname{Hom}(s_*N,M)=\operatorname{Hom}(N,s^!_0M)$. Thus $s^!_0$ is right adjoint to the exact sheaf functor $s_*$. By [lem-sp-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives], it preserves injectives. Choose a bounded-below injective representative $K\simeq I$ [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative]. Both $I$ and $s^!_0I$ are bounded-below injective complexes; [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-plus-injective] computes $SK$ by $s^!_0I$ and its global cohomology by $\Gamma(Y,s^!_0I)$.

source.place: Tag 09XQ, lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic: its Hom calculation; same calculation for the specified pro-etale support kernel

proof.text:
In each degree $r$ the sectionwise kernel formula of [def-pur-flasque-support] gives
$$\Gamma(Y,s^!_0I^r)=\Gamma(X,s_*s^!_0I^r)=\ker(I^r(X)\to I^r(U)).$$
The differentials are the restrictions of those of $I$, so this is an equality of complexes with $\Gamma_Z(X,I)$. By the definition [def-pur-support-cohomology] and the derived computation in step 6 it yields a natural isomorphism
$$R\Gamma(Y,SK)\cong R\Gamma_Z(X,K).$$
No comparison of a sheaf with a module of global sections is being made: taking degree $q+1$ gives the asserted identification of cohomology modules for every integer $q$.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support: derived supported sections and the support-sheaf construction

proof.text: The global connecting map has the prescribed normalization. The sequence $0\to s_*s^!_0I\to I\to j_*j^*I\to0$ is [lem-pur-support-exact]. Its sequence of global sections is also degreewise short exact. For surjectivity, [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] applied to $A_X$ supplies the monomorphism $j_!A_U\to A_X$. Applying $\operatorname{Hom}(-,I^r)$ is surjective by injectivity; the module map determined by $1$ identifies this map with $I^r(X)\to I^r(U)$. The kernels are those of step 7. Moreover $j^*I$ computes $j^*K$ on $U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives]. Therefore the global short exact sequence is precisely the injective-resolution sequence defining the support boundary of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness]. By the cone-triangle convention of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the triangle obtained from this sequence through the quasi-isomorphism $q:\operatorname{Cone}(u)\to j_*j^*I$, $q(b,a)=\eta_j(b)$, of [lem-pc-cone-short-exact-quasi-iso] has boundary $-p\circ q^{-1}$, $p$ the projection to $(s_*s^!_0I)[1]$. The termwise additive functor of sections over $X$ carries the cone, $q$ and $p$ to the cone, cone-to-quotient map and projection of the global sequence, and $\operatorname{Cone}(u)$ is again a bounded below complex of injectives, so this is also the derived global triangle. On cohomology: for a degree-$q$ cocycle $c$ of $\Gamma(U,j^*I)$ choose $b\in I^q(X)$ restricting to $c$; then $db$ lies in the support kernel, $(b,-db)$ is a cocycle of the cone with $q(b,-db)=c$, and $-p(b,-db)=db$. Thus the connecting morphism of the sheaf triangle induces exactly the snake boundary $[c]\mapsto[db]$ of the global short exact sequence, which is the support boundary of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], with no extra sign.

source.place: Tag 09XP, first derived triangle and following long exact sequence; cone-to-quotient normalization

proof.text:
Derived sections after direct image introduce no different arrow. A pro-etale direct image is right adjoint to exact inverse image [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], so it preserves K-injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. On a K-injective representative $J$ of any bounded-below input $L$ one therefore computes
$$R\Gamma(Y,Rf_*L)=\Gamma(Y,f_*J)=\Gamma(T,J)=R\Gamma(T,L)$$
for $f:T\to Y$; the middle equality is evaluation at the final object. It is natural for maps of representatives and hence for derived maps by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. Apply this to $p,\pi,s$. The identity $ps=\mathrm{id}$ and the composition comparison of [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] give the same first-term identification as step 7. The second arrow evaluates to restriction $\Gamma(X,I)\to\Gamma(U,j^*I)$, by step 3. Steps 5 and 8 thus prove $H^q(Y,d)=\partial$ under all the displayed global identifications.

For the edge maps, apply [lem-pe-bounded-complex-direct-image-presheaf] to $f=\mathrm{id}_Y$. For a bounded-below complex $V$ it identifies $\mathcal H^r(V)$ with the sheafification of $W\mapsto H^r(W,V)$. The sheafification map at the final object is exactly $e_V^r$: it sends a class to its local classes. This construction is natural also for derived morphisms. Indeed choose bounded-below K-injective representatives; [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] represents a derived morphism by a homotopy class of chain maps, the presheaf comparison is natural for each such chain map, and homotopic maps act equally on every section-complex cohomology. For $f:V\to V'$ this proves
$$e_{V'}^r H^r(Y,f)=\Gamma(Y,\mathcal H^r(f))e_V^r.$$
The construction commutes with shifts: cocycles and boundaries in degree $r$ of $J[1]$ are those in degree $r+1$ of $J$, since changing both differentials by $-1$ changes neither their kernels nor their images.

source.place: Tags 0D6I (lemma-unbounded-describe-higher-direct-images), 0BKV (lemma-sheafification-cohomology); apply the natural presheaf description to the identity morphism

proof.text:
Use step 10 with $V=R\pi_*j^*K$, $V'=C[1]$, $f=d$ and $r=q$. The shift identification turns $\mathcal H^q(d)$ into $\delta^q$ and $e_{C[1]}^q$ into $e_C^{q+1}$. Step 9 turns $H^q(Y,d)$ into $\partial$. Hence, for every $\alpha$,
$$e_C^{q+1}(\partial\alpha)=\Gamma(Y,\delta^q)\bigl(e_{R\pi_*j^*K}^q(\alpha)\bigr).$$
There is no restriction on the sign of $q$: the section complexes and sheaf cohomology are integer-indexed throughout.

source.place: Connecting map carrying kappa(t) to its support boundary: edge compatibility for an arbitrary class

proof.text:
Finally the etale comparison. By step 3 the triangle and its boundary $d$ are, by definition, the $
u_Y^*$-transport of the etale triangle $D	o Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}B	o R\pi_{\mathrm{et},*}j_{\mathrm{et}}^*B\xrightarrow{d_{\mathrm{et}}}D[1]$ of step 2, under the isomorphisms of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison]. The isomorphism $R\Gamma(Y_{\mathrm{et}},V)\simeq R\Gamma(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},
u_Y^*V)$ of [sk-prop-sf-comparison] for bounded-below etale $V$ is induced by the unit $V	o R
u_{Y,*}
u_Y^*V$, hence is natural in $V$ and compatible with shifts. Applied to the three etale terms it carries $H^q(Y_{\mathrm{et}},d_{\mathrm{et}})$ to $H^q(Y,d)$, which is $\partial$ by step 9, and likewise the first two arrows. Under the identification of step 7 this is the precise sense in which the support boundary and the global identifications agree with their etale counterparts. The cohomology sheaves are compared by exact inverse image (step 3), $\mathcal H^r(
u_Y^*V)=
u_Y^*\mathcal H^r(V)$, and the edge map sends a class to its local classes (step 10). Restriction and the comparison unit are natural: on an etale object $W	o Y$ the comparison takes the restricted etale class to the corresponding restricted pro-etale class, so the presheaf-to-sheaf maps commute with it. These local equalities give equality of the resulting sheaf sections. Thus the boundary, the edge formula and all displayed identifications agree with their ordinary etale counterparts.

split_report.summary: Expanded the retracted closed-support comparison into twelve steps using existing nodes only. Distinguished the transported finite exceptional inverse image from the ambient pro-etale support adjoint; proved their comparison on etale-origin objects via the counit transpose and a morphism of localization triangles. Computed supported sections on injectives, fixed the global boundary sign by the same cone-to-quotient map, and obtained the integer-degree edge formula from local-class naturality. No statement change or new node. Maintainer reader (Q157): step 1 now cites exactness of the closed direct image on the etale site for Rs_* = s_*; step 8 writes out the -p q^{-1} boundary computation against the snake boundary; step 12 states precisely the etale comparison it proves.
